themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints spiked to 9 THIS WEEK compared to 0.8 per week baseline—a 1100% increase (z-score: 7.57)—suggesting possible service disruption or contractor failure in Flatbush/Prospect Heights.
evidence: 9 street sweeping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike, z-score: 7.57)
Complaint volume represents statistically significant anomaly flagged as high severity
No prior context in news or community board data, suggesting sudden service failure
reporting_angles: Call NYC Sanitation to determine if a contractor was pulled, routes were consolidated, or equipment failed
Canvass residents on affected blocks to document street conditions and timeline of decline

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK from 0.4 weekly average—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.42)—indicating possible shift in dog-owner behavior or enforcement gap in parks.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
High z-score indicates statistically anomalous event, not random variation
Aligns with community board priority on park access and amenities; possible enforcement resource gap
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Enforcement officers about staffing levels and response times at district parks
Talk to dog owners and park-goers to understand whether leash violations have genuinely increased or are being reported more

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Wave Last Week
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints hit 22 LAST WEEK, up 552% from 3.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.12), suggesting possible coordinated tagging activity or reduced NYPD/Parks response.
evidence: 22 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (552% spike, z-score: 5.12)
High statistical severity and z-score flagged in official spike analysis
Geographic concentration in one district suggests localized problem, not city-wide trend
reporting_angles: Canvas commercial corridors (Nostrand, Flatbush, Church Ave) to identify whether tags are concentrated or distributed
Ask NYPD/Parks about abatement response times and whether crews were diverted to other areas last week

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicles Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints jumped to 19 LAST WEEK from 7.8 weekly average—a 145% increase (z-score: 8.08)—indicating possible abandoned car dump or towing service backlog.
evidence: 19 derelict vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 7.8 weekly baseline (145% spike, z-score: 8.08)
Spike correlates with broader illegal parking complaints (2073 over 90 days, top 3 category)
High z-score suggests this is not baseline neighborhood problem but sudden event
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with NYPD towing records to identify streets with most abandoned vehicles
Interview NYPD Traffic and Sanitation about towing capacity and whether a contractor is behind schedule

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Spike (3 Weeks Ago)
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints reached 11 THREE WEEKS AGO, up 1367% from 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 9.41)—highest statistical anomaly in dataset—likely tied to construction activity; urgency depends on whether complaints continue.
evidence: 11 asbestos complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 weekly average (1367% spike, highest z-score: 9.41)
338 active DOB building permits (191 alterations) in district—alterations are known asbestos exposure vector
No follow-up spike data provided; unclear if problem persists or was isolated event
reporting_angles: Request DOB records showing which buildings filed asbestos notifications 3 weeks ago; cross-reference with permit filings
Interview NYC Department of Environmental Protection about asbestos abatement enforcement and whether any violations were issued
